chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Silver for silver, like for like, with no increase and no decrease; the one who adds and the one who seeks addition are in the Fire."

key_terms.اَلزَّائِدُ: The one who adds (the extra amount)
key_terms.اَلْفِضَّةُ: Silver (used here as a type of currency/thaman)
key_terms.اَلْمُسْتَزِيدُ: The one who seeks the increase
key_terms.مِثْلاً بِمِثْلٍ: Like for like / equal for equal

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging silver for silver with a slight increase in weight according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* specifies the application of *mithlan bi mithlin* (equal for equal) strictly to silver, establishing it as a primary medium of exchange where no increase is permitted in spot transactions. It highlights the reciprocal nature of riba by punishing both the giver and taker of the excess, a principle deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between commodity and currency exchanges. The prohibition underscores the spiritual danger of riba, linking the financial transgression directly to eternal punishment in the Fire.
